title: Configuration Modes
levelTitle: Level 28 - Cisco IOS and IOS XE

cards.q: How is IOS configuration organized into modes?
cards.a: IOS uses a hierarchy: global config, then interface, line, or router modes, then nested submodes. Each prompt reflects the current context, and commands apply only to that mode's scope.

cards.q: How do you tell which configuration mode you are in?
cards.a: Read the prompt: # is privileged EXEC, (config)# is global config, (config-if)# is interface, (config-line)# is line, and (config-router)# is router configuration.

cards.q: Which commands take you from privileged EXEC to global, interface, line, and router modes?
cards.a: configure terminal enters global config; from global, interface Gi0/1 enters interface mode, line console 0 enters line mode, and router ospf 1 enters router mode. Submodes always nest under global config.

cards.q: What is the difference between exit, end, and Ctrl+Z?
cards.a: exit goes up one mode level, while end and Ctrl+Z go all the way back to privileged EXEC mode.

cards.q: You are in interface config and type interface Gi0/2. What happens?
cards.a: The prompt switches context directly to the new interface without requiring you to exit to global config first.

cards.q: Which commands apply device-wide in global config?
cards.a: hostname, ip route, access-list, snmp-server, and logging are global commands that affect the whole device.

cards.q: Which commands are scoped to a single interface under (config-if)?
cards.a: ip address, no shutdown, description, speed and duplex, and channel-group apply only to that interface.

cards.q: Give the command session to assign an IP and bring up an interface, then return to EXEC.
cards.a: configure terminal; interface GigabitEthernet0/1; ip address 10.0.0.1 255.255.255.0; no shutdown; then end or Ctrl+Z.

cards.q: What does the do command allow inside config mode?
cards.a: The do command runs EXEC commands such as show or ping from inside configuration mode so you can verify settings without exiting.

cards.q: A configuration command is rejected. What do you check first?
cards.a: Your mode and prompt. A config command entered in privileged EXEC, or an EXEC command entered in config mode without do, is rejected; read the prompt and exit or use do as needed.
